replace._note: Armoury 1915 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): limestone entry block with two towers, brick drill hall with gambrel roof (drawn as gable)
60 Victoria St E, Christ Church (Anglican) 1846 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): red brick, cross plan, no steeple
54 Victoria St E, County Court House 1888 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): sandstone, 2.5 storeys, Romanesque arched windows, no tower

replace.label: Dominion Building
replace._note: 98 Victoria St E, Dominion Public Building 1934-36 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): light grey sandstone front, two storeys. East wall: North Nova Scotia Highlanders memorial mural (WWII), an original simplified panel.
66 Victoria St E, First Baptist 1895 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): red sandstone, two tall turreted towers

replace.label: Old Post Office
replace._note: 50 Victoria St E, old post office and customs 1884-86 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): red and grey sandstone, 2.5 storeys, Gothic windows, central clock tower with cupola
91 Victoria St E, butcher shop 1897 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): red sandstone, two storeys, arched upper windows

replace.label: Bank
replace._note: 79 Victoria St E, old Bank of Nova Scotia 1907 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): smooth red sandstone, one tall storey, round windows
1 Ratchford St, Trinity-St. Stephen's United 1906 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): red sandstone, square castellated bell tower

replace.label: Station
replace._note: Station St, railway station 1907-08 (Canadian Register of Historic Places): rock-faced red sandstone, 1.5 storeys, steep hipped roof

177 Victoria St E, 1907 (Canadian Register of Historic Places + from reference photos): white shingles, wrap-around veranda, stone turret and round bays; outline simplified to its bounding rectangle so it can take the hipped roof

233 Victoria St E main house c.1845 (Canadian Register of Historic Places + reference photos): two-storey Classical Revival, light blue clapboard, gable end to the street, corner pilasters; the wing and garage wing are custom buildings
start house: 1.5-storey Cape, light blue siding, steep shingle gable, brick chimney
Norman St Cape Cod (from reference photos): white Cape Cod, green asphalt roof, two front gabled dormers, centred door with sidelights, navy shutters; LiDAR top ~7.7 m
Hastings Rd house (reference photos + LiDAR footprint): grey single storey, low gable, deck and steps out front, gravel loop drive
Penny Lane home (reference photos): red brick ground floor, cream siding above, brown gable roof, covered front porch, teal shutters
Harding Ave home (reference photos + LiDAR pyramid roof): two-storey foursquare, taupe shingles, tan hip roof; the front 8.2 m of the OSM outline
LaPlanche St (9, by the civic file; the mural is listed near 7): 'The Great Amherst Mystery' mural on the wall facing the lot towards Victoria St, an original simplified panel (placed approximately)
